title: Checklist 1

lessons.title: Course Material: Checklist-1.pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Email Copywriting Essentials – Summary Checklist  ü Email marketing is one of the most powerful forms of communicating with customers ü We’re going to be focusing on the essentials of what you need to do to write engaging, high-converting emails  Learning Objectives: By the end, you’ll be able to: ü Identify the 3 main types of marketing emails ü Send the right type of email for a particular marketing message ü Employ best practices to meet your business goals with your emails ü Choose the right email content to satisfy your customer's needs ü Increase sales and profits without ‘selling’ in your emails ü Write powerful email subject lines that boost your open rates ü Create compelling calls to action in your emails ü Create an action plan that implements your new email copywriting skills   Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  Module 1 – Why Good Email Copy is Essential to Your Marketing Success  ü Quality of copy is critical for success ü What you write can engage & satisfy customers, as well as help you meet your goals  Why Most People Don’t Spend Enough Time Writing Their Marketing Emails 1. They don’t know what to do ü Some business owners don’t know where to begin ü They don’t understand how email marketing systems work ü They skip sending out emails all together 2. They hate to sell ü A lot of successful business owners despise the sales process ü Learn to engage and inform through emails  ü Do little actual selling 3. They underestimate the importance of great copy in emails ü You may understand the power of copywriting ü Don’t underestimate the power of persuasive copy in emails ü Well written copy is essential in any communication

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Writing Powerful Emails Develops a One-to-One Relationship ü Copy is vital in the nature of the relationships you develop ü Subscribers expect to be treated as an individual ü They respond better if your emails speak to their needs and desires  Great Email Copy Should be Personal ü Personalize to your customers’ needs ü Get to know your ‘perfect’ customer ü Create emotionally engaging copy  Meet AIDA, Your Email Copywriting Formula ü Attention ü Interest ü Desire  ü Action ü Adhere to this formula to virtually guarantee email marketing success  Action Step: 1. Take a look at a few of your latest marketing emails or a recent email marketing campaign. Evaluate those emails and take notes on where you think you can improve them overall by applying the AIDA formula:  • A - Getting the customers attention  • I - Building their interest • D - Creating their desire and  • A - Getting your reader to take action

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  Module 2 – The Three Key Types of Emails and Their Benefits  ü There are three types of emails you’ll send to prospective customers: o Broadcast emails o Transactional emails o Autoresponder emails ü All 3 have different goals and structure ü They will all be more effective with good copy  Broadcast Emails ü A message you manually send to all or a group of subscribers ü Generally only used to convey one-time information ü There is almost always some kind of time-sensitive characteristic ü Examples include: o One-time sales o Promotional events o Seasonal announcements o New product launch  o Changes in store hours, business expansion or new additions to the company ü Emails can be sent to everyone, or just a group  Transactional Emails ü ‘Behaviour triggered’ – Sent when some type of transaction occurs ü E.g. A sales receipt ü Examples include: o Product request notification

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  o Order confirmation o Customer service communication ü Change urgency to their side of the email communication ü Offer a special or discount ü Appeal to customers looking to save money  Autoresponder Emails ü An email marketer’s best friend ü Your first email goes out as soon as someone signs up to your list ü Thank subscribers for joining and let them know what to expect from you ü Autoresponders allow you to schedule a series of emails in advance ü Schedule the next emails according to length of time a subscriber has been signed-up for ü Build relationships using software so you don’t have to manually send out emails  Why You Should Periodically Evaluate Your Autoresponder Series ü You can test different parts of your sequence and make improvements ü Look at your emails after a while and see which is performing best ü Tweak other emails that aren’t performing as well ü Give your changes a chance to perform ü You can try re-evaluating every month, or quarter ü Test results  What Makes for a Good Autoresponder Email? ü There are many different needs and desires ü There are some things that can be found in many emails that are

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  generally successful ü Examples include: o Focus on the reader o Solve problems without asking for a sale o Always provides value ü A ‘good’ autoresponder email depends on different variables ü Make an offer or ask for a sale in 25% of emails ü Consider your unique subscriber base  Use Autoresponders to Move Your Subscriber through Your Sales Funnel ü The sales process used to be physical ü Using automated tools, you can effortlessly move subscribers along a funnel ü You’ll need to constantly evaluate to figure out the best fit for your customers ü An example would include: o Thank you email o Reminder email o Value-packed content  Which Autoresponder Service Should I Use? ü Examples include: o Aweber o ActiveCampaign o GetResponse o Constant Contact  o MailChimp ü All companies provide excellent tools and customer support ü Monitor, create and send emails

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  ü Also measure effectiveness   Action Steps: 1. List ideas for broadcast emails you might send to your list based on time-sensitive events that occur in your business 2. Make a list of the transactional emails you currently send, including ones that you write after people have purchased a product 3. Make a list of any autoresponder series that you currently have, and ones which you’d like to add or expand

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Module 3 – What Should You Write About in Your Emails?  ü For many people, writing is the most difficult part ü They may have everything laid out, but still get writers’ block ü Determine what you should be writing about first  Who am I Writing To? ü May seem like a simple question, but might not be ü Write as if it were directed to an individual ü Think about your ‘perfect customer’ ü Spend time on this thought process ü It doesn’t matter what type of email ü Look at all info at your disposal  What do I Know about My Products and Services? ü Focus on what you know about your business ü What do you have to offer? ü What solutions can your products and services offer your customers?  Am I Writing to Sell or to Inform? ü There is nothing wrong with selling something ü Don’t sell in each of your emails ü Offer valuable, free information

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  What did I Talk about in the Last Few Emails? ü Look at your entire series ü If you’ve provided lots of free informational emails, it might be time for a promotional one ü If not, you could send more info or thank your customers  What are my Current Business Needs? ü Tailor your emails to your immediate goals ü An example would be bundled product sales ü If sales have been good, send out a thank you and a reward  What are my Competitors Writing About? ü Get on your competitors mailing lists to find out what they’re writing about ü Look at the times they send out emails ü Also look at the subject lines they use  Is there any Time-Sensitive Information I Need to Convey? ü Think about any upcoming holidays ü Do a search online to see what’s happening ü Figure out a way to tie your products and services in with random holidays  What Have My Readers Asked for? ü Listen to your subscribers ü Systematically send out surveys

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  ü Look for patterns in problems and opportunities  What Problems, Needs and Desires Do My Readers Have? ü As long as you can solve problems, you will always have a viable business ü This doesn’t have to be a sales-oriented email ü Show subscribers you think of them as people with real needs  Am I Writing for the Right Reason? ü You might catch yourself writing an email just for the sake of it ü This is always a bad decision ü Find something that will bring value to the reader while also helping your business    Action Steps: 1. Outline key points for a broadcast email for a seasonal sale, product, event, news item, or promotion. Note the specifics of the main topic of the email (e.g., if it’s a product promotion), who it is targeting, and how you are meeting a solution 2. Add a Tips and Tricks section for one of the transactional emails you listed in the previous module. Include important information for the product your customers are purchasing 3. Outline the topics for 5 follow-up autoresponder emails you will write for one of your products or services. Draw from the topic ideas in the module for ideas of what to write about

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11  Module 4 – How to Write Your Emails for Maximum Impact and Conversion ü Engaging emails are all about structure ü There is a proven formula to deliver readers to your call to action ü Important steps include: o From name o Subject line o Pre-header o Body o Close o Signature o P.S.  From Name ü You treat personal mail differently to that of a business ü People prefer to receive email from an individual ü Think about how ‘friendly’ your email address is  Subject Line ü Keep your subject line short
